title: 2025 is the Year of Evals! Just like 2024, and 2023, and … — John Dickerson, CEO Mozilla AI
talk_summary: A market/enterprise-adoption talk arguing that evals are finally a budget priority because agentic systems take autonomous actions and executives now demand quantitative risk numbers. The only concrete technical content is in the Q&A: expert-in-the-loop validation for domain-heavy agent outputs, and LLM-as-judge with known biases that must itself be validated.

takeaways.technique: Expert-in-the-loop validation for high-stakes agent output
takeaways.what_they_do: Pair a domain expert with the multi-agent system to do expensive human validation in lockstep, especially where errors are costly (e.g. financial analysis).
takeaways.numbers: $50/hr, $100/hr, $200/hr expert rates cited from a leaked spreadsheet

takeaways.what_they_do: Use LLM-as-judge to solve dataset creation, but explicitly check the judge against human labels because judges carry biases (conciseness, helpfulness, persona effects).
takeaways.evidence_quote: you do need to make sure you're validating this and and making sure that you're not going off in some weird bias direction

takeaways.technique: Build task-specific eval environments as capex
takeaways.what_they_do: Invest in a good domain environment/dataset (e.g. a DCF environment) as a durable asset that differentiates you versus competitors.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's the data set creation and the environment creation that matters more than anything

takeaways.technique: Monitor the whole system, not one model
takeaways.what_they_do: Shift observability from single-model metrics to end-to-end multi-agent system monitoring.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You shouldn't just monitor the one model that is being used by one particular agent.
